references.text: Both verses describe the same sequence of events (Pharaoh's anger and the imprisonment) from different perspectives in the narrative.
The verses form the beginning and end of the same conflict: Pharaoh's anger initiates the imprisonment (40:2), while that same anger leads to the execution of the baker (40:20).
The verses illuminate each other through the contrast between Pharaoh's initial anger and the final mercy shown to the cupbearer.
The verse contains details of the dream that directly led to the baker becoming the object of Pharaoh's anger mentioned in the source verse.
